task: Security: stop logging bearer tokens and PII (audit HIGH-02); require message-group membership to read or post a DM (audit HIGH-01)

context.why_logging: Container stdout goes to CloudWatch (/cruddur/CrdService, 14-day retention). Before this spec, app.py printed 50 characters of every Authorization header and, on /api/activities, every header in full; lib/db.py printed every SQL statement with its params (message text, Cognito IDs); messages.py printed whole conversations; the post-confirmation Lambda printed email and name; the upload-avatar and authorizer Lambdas printed the full event including the token. Anyone with log read access could replay a live token for up to an hour.
context.why_membership: GET /api/messages/<uuid> and POST /api/messages (update mode) served any message_group_uuid to any signed-in user. messages.py already looked up my_user_uuid and then never used it. The fix: Ddb.is_member queries the caller's own GRP#<uuid> partition for a row with that message_group_uuid. It uses the base table with ConsistentRead (not the GSI, which is eventually consistent and could wrongly reject a just-created group), sets no Limit (Limit is applied before FilterExpression and could hide the match), and paginates.
context.status_code: Non-members get 404 message_group_not_found rather than 403, so the API does not confirm that a given group exists.
context.sql_debug: print_sql and print_params now print only when the env var CRUDDUR_SQL_DEBUG=1. It is not set in ECS. Set it locally when you need SQL traces. print_sql_err is unchanged: errors still print.
context.lambdas: The three Lambda edits change repo source ONLY. Nothing is redeployed by this spec. How each Lambda is packaged (CrdAuth for post-confirmation; manual zips with gem/node dependencies for upload-avatar and the authorizer) must be checked before redeploying, because uploading a bare file without its dependencies would break it.
context.tested: Claude applied these exact edits to reconstructions of the files and ran them. The membership check allows a member found on the second page of results, rejects non-members on both read and post, sets ConsistentRead with no Limit, and passes ExclusiveStartKey when paginating. Python ast.parse, node --check and ruby -c all pass on the edited snippets.
context.overlap: The later kiro-spec-hardening.json edits query_commit and print_sql_err in lib/db.py and the LOGGER line in app.py. This spec touches none of those lines, so hardening's anchors remain valid.
context.edit_method: Every change is an exact find-and-replace. 'old' must occur EXACTLY ONCE in the named file and is replaced by 'new'. Indentation is significant: app.py mixes 4-space routes (data_messages) and 2-space routes (data_create_message). Use the IDE file-edit tool.

edits.id: MSG_A: membership check before list_messages; stop printing message bodies
edits.old:
ddb = Ddb.client()
    data = Ddb.list_messages(ddb, message_group_uuid)
    print("list_messages")
    print(data)
edits.new:
ddb = Ddb.client()
    # Audit HIGH-01: only a participant may read this conversation.
    # my_user_uuid was already looked up above but was never used.
    if my_user_uuid is None or not Ddb.is_member(ddb, message_group_uuid, my_user_uuid):
      model['errors'] = ['message_group_not_found']
      return model
    data = Ddb.list_messages(ddb, message_group_uuid)
    # Audit HIGH-02: print a count, not the private message bodies.
    print(f"list_messages: {len(data)} items")

verify_next_deploy: Logs: after exercising the app in pilot #3, run the three commands below. Each prints only a COUNT, never the log text, and each should be 0: `aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /cruddur/CrdService --filter-pattern '"Auth header"' --query 'length(events)'`, the same with '"Headers:"', and the same with '"SQL Params"'.
DM read, own conversation: signed in as user A, open a conversation from the Messages page. It loads (200).

DM read, someone else's: take a message_group_uuid that A belongs to (it is in the URL). Signed in as a DIFFERENT account B that is not in that conversation, GET /api/messages/<that uuid> with B's token. Expect 404 ['message_group_not_found']. Load tokens with read -s TOKEN and unset TOKEN afterwards; never paste a token into chat.
DM post, someone else's: as B, POST /api/messages {message_group_uuid: <A's uuid>, message: 'x'}. Expect 404, and A's conversation shows no new message.
New conversation: A starts a NEW conversation from the Messages page. It opens immediately with the first message (no 404). This proves ConsistentRead covers the just-created case.
Random uuid: GET /api/messages/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 with A's token. Expect 404.
